items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, what about a guy that's like that? Ray Lopez down here. Would he play straight melody, or would he be a get-off man, or what? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, oh, that's... It was in between. He had his own style.

ctx.x: See, like, like over in England, you see over there? Mm-hmm. Well, when we first went over there, you had to play melody, see? Mm-hmm. The trumpet had to play melody. Mm-hmm. If they didn't hear the melody, they were out. They want to hear a melody, see? Then the others fill in around, but carry the melody. That's what they want to hear. As long as they hear that melody, they know what you're playing. But if they hear a lot of, uh, a lot of notes, they don't know what it's all about. They can't understand one…
Well, what about a guy that's like that? Ray Lopez down here. Would he play straight melody, or would he be a get-off man, or what? Well, he would be a...

Oh, oh, that's... It was in between. He had his own style. Emil had his own style, and, uh, those days Johnny Detroit was around, he had his own style, and Brunus had his own style. Everybody had their particular style.
